transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep getting stuck checking things at home. Outlets, locks, tools, even dust… I go over them again and again, trying to fix or make sure everything is right. It takes up most of my day, and even when I’m worn out, I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, aside from the need to check things?

Yes. Even when I know I did something right, I get these awful thoughts that maybe I missed a loose wire and the house could burn down, or that I left a nail somewhere and my wife might get hurt. I try to push the thoughts away, but they just come back harder.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or order?

Yes, kind of. I don’t know if it’s always a set order, but I get stuck going back over the same things—outlets, locks, tools, dust—and I keep checking or fixing them again and again. I can spend most of the day doing that until I’m worn out, and even then I still don’t feel sure enough to stop.
Are you trying to prevent something bad from happening when you do these checks?

Yes. That’s what it feels like. I keep going back over the outlets, locks, tools, and even dust because I’m trying to make sure nothing bad happens. I check and fix things again and again, most of the day sometimes, and even when I’m exhausted I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel less anxious after you've completed one of these checking routines?

Maybe for a minute, but not really in a way that lasts. I’ll check the outlets or locks or the tools, and I think I should be done, but then I still don’t feel sure. So I go back and do it again, and again, until I’m worn out. It takes up most of my day sometimes.
Do you feel like you need to check things a certain number of times to feel okay about stopping?

Not really a certain number, no. It’s more that I keep going back over the same things—outlets, locks, tools, dust—and I don’t feel sure enough to stop. I’ll check or fix something, then doubt it, and do it again until I’m worn out.
Do you feel like you have to arrange things in a specific way, like keeping your tools or other items in a particular order?

Yeah, mostly with my tools and things around the house. It’s not like they have to be in some perfect order, but I keep checking them and fixing them, moving them back, making sure they’re right. Same with outlets, locks, even dust. I go over it again and again, and it takes up most of my day sometimes. I end up worn out and still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
Are these checking behaviors and thoughts affecting your relationships or work?

Yeah, it has. I stopped taking paid carpentry jobs because I can’t get out of the house and get through a day normally. I used to help with community projects too, but I’ve pulled back from that.

My wife has had to take on more errands and decisions because I get stuck checking things at home, and by the time I’m done I’m just exhausted.
Do you feel like the tools or items you check need to be in a perfect or symmetrical order?

Not really perfect or symmetrical, no. It’s more that I keep going back to the same things—my tools, outlets, locks, dust—and checking or fixing them again and again. I just don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone, and I end up worn out from it.
Do you ever feel like you need to repeat a checking action a certain number of times before you can stop?

Not really a certain number, no. It’s more that I keep going back over the same things—outlets, locks, my tools, dust—and checking or fixing them again and again until I’m worn out. I just still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like the things you check or arrange need to be 'just right' in some way?

Not exactly “just right” like neat or perfect. It’s more like I can’t trust that it’s okay. I keep going back to the outlets, locks, tools, and dust, checking or fixing them again and again until I’m worn out, and even then I still don’t really feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like you have to repeat these checking actions in exactly the same way each time?

Not exactly in the same way each time. It’s more that I keep getting pulled back to the same things—outlets, locks, tools, dust—and I check them or fix them over and over. I can spend most of the day doing that, and even when I’m worn out, I still don’t feel sure enough to stop.
Are you ever worried about germs or getting sick when you're checking these things at home?
No, I don’t think it’s really about germs or getting sick. At least, that’s not what I notice. It’s more just… I don’t feel sure, so I check again.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be in a specific pattern or arrangement?

Not really a specific pattern or arrangement. It’s more that I keep going back over the same things—outlets, locks, tools, dust—checking or fixing them again and again. I can spend most of the day doing it, and even when I’m worn out, I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you ever have thoughts about harming yourself or someone else?

I don’t want to hurt myself or anybody else. But I do get these ugly thoughts, like… even when I know I fixed something right, I suddenly think maybe I missed a loose wire and the house will burn down, or I left a nail somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I try to push it out of my head, but it comes back stronger.
Do you feel like the things you check or fix have to be symmetrical or look a certain way for you to feel okay about stopping?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it being about symmetry or how it looks, exactly. It’s more just whether I can feel okay enough to stop, and I usually can’t.
Do you feel like the things you check need to be arranged in a way that looks or feels complete to you?

Not really arranged, no. It’s not like I need things lined up a certain way. I just keep going back to the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust, checking or fixing them over and over. It takes up most of my day, and even when I’m exhausted, I still don’t feel sure enough to stop.
Do you feel like you have to repeat these checking actions until you feel like you've done them a certain number of times?

Not really a number, no. I’m not counting like that. It’s more that I keep going back to the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust, checking and fixing them again and again until I’m worn out. And even then I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.

Not really in a very exact way, no. It’s more that I keep going back over the same things — the outlets, locks, tools, dust — checking or fixing them again and again. I get worn out doing it, but I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
